result.strongest_objection: Generation-only completion fencing is insufficient. The design permits up to three at-least-once RunJob calls in one generation, yet every resulting child emits the same generation value. If an earlier ambiguously accepted attempt completes after a later attempt, `FinishTaskIfActive` accepts whichever completion reaches the CAS first. Different results can therefore win based on timing, violating deterministic behavior and leaving same-generation stale writers unfenced.
result.catch: The acceptance and race plans cover prior-generation and duplicate completions but omit conflicting completions from different reservations within the same generation—the exact case created by timeout/crash recovery after an accepted RunJob.
result.proposed_fix: Propagate `reservation_id` and attempt through `DispatchParams`, `AILANG_DISPATCH_RESERVATION_ID`, and `TaskCompletion`. Persist a completion-authority token and require `FinishTaskIfActive` to match both generation and the currently authorized reservation. Define explicitly when a newer reservation supersedes an older one and whether completion from an ambiguously failed reservation remains eligible. Add barrier tests where attempt 1 is accepted but appears failed, attempt 2 is reserved, and both return conflicting completions; the specified authoritative reservation must win regardless of completion arrival order.
